claims.text: As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
Pack-cementation aluminizing of as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will form a thin, adherent alumina scale.
The alumina scale produced by aluminizing will significantly improve high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The aluminizing treatment can improve oxygen resistance without degrading the alloy's inherent ductility or yield strength.
Treatment at approximately 1000 °C for 4 hours in an aluminum-rich pack under inert gas will produce the intended aluminized surface.
A brief oxidation step at 900–1000 °C will promote formation of the protective alumina layer.
Aluminizing will form a thin, adherent aluminum-enriched intermetallic interlayer.
The aluminum-enriched interlayer will oxidize to produce a continuous, dense Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Suppressing oxygen diffusion through the surface scale will protect the bulk alloy from oxidation and preserve its microstructural integrity.
After exposure in air at 1000 °C for up to 100 hours, the treated alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
After exposure in air at 1000 °C for up to 100 hours, the treated alloy will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Excessive aluminization may form brittle intermetallic phases or a deep aluminum diffusion zone.
Brittle intermetallic phases or excessive aluminum diffusion may degrade local surface ductility.
